artifacts.summary: Re-verifies all six Tier B phantom/missing-row inventory tables, traces every phantom row to its Boneyard archive location, decides obsolete-vs-re-home per row, and finds a new issue not named in the dispatch: WitnessFamily/README.md's lower table duplicates Sharing/README.md's own current table with stale pre-refactor content.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo's check-module-invariants.sh --emit-inventory generator, a phantom inventory row (naming a file that no longer exists at that path) is dropped automatically on regeneration if the file was moved rather than deleted outright -- the pinned-row logic only keeps a non-scanned key when os.path.isfile() resolves it relative to the CURRENT scan directory, so a file relocated to Boneyard/ (archived) no longer resolves and the row vanishes with no manual deletion needed. The only required human judgment is deciding, before wrapping, whether the row's hand-written description is worth re-homing onto a live sibling file (check sibling docstrings for topical overlap first) or is simply obsolete.

When a top-level README's inventory table duplicates a nested subdirectory's own README table (same directory, same file set, same Lines column), check whether the nested README's table is itself already wrapped and current before treating the duplicate as a simple re-keying fix -- the duplicate's descriptions can be stale in CONTENT (describing a pre-refactor architecture), not just counts, and the nested table is the authoritative source to resync from. Two independently-generated blocks pointed at the same directory will not stay in sync with each other going forward (check-module-invariants.sh's INV check only verifies a block against its own directory's live files, never cross-block consistency), which is an accepted trade-off matching this repo's existing top-level-summary-plus-nested-README convention (e.g. Compression/), not a defect to eliminate.
